p185.002: A little after six o'clock on the morning of Friday, April 7, A.D. 30, Jesus was brought with his hands bound before Pilate, the Roman governor. About fifty accusers went along, including Caiaphas, members of the Sanhedrin, and Judas Iscariot, and so did the apostle John. The Jewish leaders believed that entering a gentile's building on the day of preparation for the Passover would make them unclean, so they would not go inside the governor's residence, and the trial was held on the steps outside the gate. The Urantia Book points out that while they were trying to kill an innocent man, they were carefully keeping their rules of purity, and it says they are not the only people who cling to small formalities and miss the duties that truly matter.
p185.004: Pilate was a capable administrator, but morally he was a coward. He did not understand the faith the Jews were willing to die for, so he clashed with them badly several times, as when he tried to bring military standards bearing Caesar's image into Jerusalem, or to build an aqueduct with money from the temple treasury. Each time he backed down in the end, so the Jewish leaders learned that they could shake him just by threatening a revolt or threatening to report him to the emperor.
p185.005: Pilate was later removed as governor for massacring Samaritans, and he never escaped the guilt of having agreed to Jesus' crucifixion. His wife, Claudia, on the other hand, heard about Jesus and later devoted herself to spreading the gospel. The Urantia Book says that if Rome had sent a better governor, this tragedy would not have happened.
p185.007: When Pilate asked what crime they were charging him with, the leaders at first did not even name a specific charge, saying, “⟦Q 185:2.1⟧If this man were not an evildoer, we should not have delivered him up to you⟦/Q⟧”. When Pilate said he would not put anyone to death without a trial, only then did they hand him a written charge: that Jesus had corrupted the nation and stirred up rebellion, that he taught people not to pay taxes to Caesar, and that he called himself king of the Jews.
p185.008: Jesus had never been tried on these charges, yet he gave no answer at all. He did not look at his accusers with scorn, but with deep pity and sad affection. Pilate was deeply impressed by his dignified, quiet manner, so he decided to take Jesus inside and question him privately.
p185.010: Pilate had Jesus sit down and asked him about the taxes, and John testified that Jesus and the apostles had always paid their taxes to Caesar and to the temple. When asked whether he was a king, Jesus answered, “⟦Q 185:3.3⟧Do you not perceive that my kingdom is not of this world?⟦/Q⟧” Jesus' kingdom, he explained, is the brotherhood of people who have become sons and daughters of God through faith and by love, and it is open to both Jews and gentiles. Jesus said he had come into this world to show the Father to all people and to bear witness to the truth, and Pilate, half mocking, asked back, “⟦Q 185:3.5⟧what is truth⟦/Q⟧”.
p185.011: Pilate was convinced that Jesus was not a dangerous revolutionary, so he went outside and declared that he found no fault in him. But when the leaders protested fiercely, saying that Jesus had been stirring up the people ever since Galilee, Pilate tried to escape responsibility by sending Jesus to Herod, the ruler of Galilee.
p185.013: Herod Antipas wanted to see Jesus perform a miracle with his own eyes. He did not remember that Jesus was the boy who, as a youth, had stood before him in Sepphoris to ask for the wages owed to his father, who had died there unjustly. Herod questioned him for about fifteen minutes and mocked him, telling him to show a miracle, but Jesus did not answer a single word. In the end Herod sneered at Jesus, put an old purple royal robe on him, and sent him back to Pilate. Herod, who had been tormented by fear ever since he killed John the Baptist, was freed from that fear only when he saw that Jesus was a completely different man from John.
p185.015: Pilate again said that Jesus was innocent and offered to have him whipped and then release him. Just then a crowd came streaming in, following the custom of releasing one prisoner at the Passover, so Pilate tried to use this chance to free Jesus and asked them whom he should release, the murderer and robber Barabbas or Jesus. But when the chief priests led the way shouting, “⟦Q 185:5.4⟧Barabbas, Barabbas!⟦/Q⟧” the crowd joined in. The people who had followed Jesus like a hero only a few days before no longer respected Jesus as he stood bound and unresisting.
p185.016: At that moment his wife, Claudia, sent him a letter: “⟦Q 185:5.8⟧I pray you have nothing to do with this innocent and just man⟦/Q⟧”. While Pilate hesitated, the leaders stirred up the crowd even more, and no matter how many times Pilate asked, the crowd only shouted, “⟦Q 185:5.9⟧Crucify him! Crucify him!⟦/Q⟧” Pilate knew Jesus was innocent, but he did not have the courage to go against the angry people.
p185.018: Jesus' friends either had not yet heard of his arrest or were hiding in fear, and the only people there were Jesus' enemies and a crowd that was easily swayed. To appeal to their pity, Pilate had Jesus whipped, which was against Roman law as well. The soldiers put a crown of thorns on him, put a reed in his hand, and mocked him, saying, “⟦Q 185:6.2⟧Hail, king of the Jews!⟦/Q⟧”
p185.019: Pilate brought out Jesus, covered in blood, and cried, “⟦Q 185:6.3⟧Behold the man!⟦/Q⟧” But the hearts of the people, gripped by hatred and prejudice, were not moved; instead they shouted even louder for crucifixion. When the high priest said Jesus must die because he had called himself the Son of God, Pilate began to tremble with fear that Jesus might really be a divine being.
p185.021: Pilate asked Jesus, “⟦Q 185:7.1⟧Where do you come from?⟦/Q⟧” but Jesus was silent. When Pilate said he had the power to release him or to crucify him, Jesus said that he would have no such power unless it were given from above, and that the sin of those who had betrayed and handed him over was greater than Pilate's. When Pilate again tried to set Jesus free, Caiaphas threatened him: “⟦Q 185:7.5⟧If you release this man, you are not Caesar's friend⟦/Q⟧”. The leaders even shouted, “⟦Q 185:7.5⟧We have no king but Caesar⟦/Q⟧”, and Pilate completely gave way out of fear of losing his position.
p185.023: Jesus was about to be handed over to death with no formal charge, no evidence, no witnesses, and no verdict. Afraid of a riot, Pilate released Barabbas, washed his hands with water, and said, “⟦Q 185:8.2⟧I am innocent of the blood of this man⟦/Q⟧”. But washing your hands does not make your responsibility disappear. Pilate, who knew what was right but backed away out of fear, reminds us how important it is to have the courage to stand on the side of what is right.
p186.002: Before Jesus was taken to Herod, he asked John, “⟦Q 186:0.1⟧Go to my mother and bring her to see me ere I die⟦/Q⟧”. John did not want to leave his Master alone, but he hurried straight to the home of Lazarus in Bethany, where Jesus' family had gathered. When she heard the news, his mother, Mary, set out with John, and his sister Ruth and his brother Jude went along too. The rest of the family stayed in Bethany, waiting for the news David Zebedee would send. By the time Mary reached the city, Jesus had already arrived at Golgotha (the place of crucifixion).
p186.004: Around half past eight in the morning, when Pilate's trial was over, Judas Iscariot appeared before the Sanhedrin and asked for his reward. He expected to be praised and honored for doing a great service for the nation, but the high priest's servant only called him out of the council chamber and handed him a bag with thirty pieces of silver. That was the price of a slave at the time. Judas felt deeply humiliated and disappointed.
p186.005: When Judas saw from a distance the cross being raised with Jesus nailed to it, he rushed back to the Sanhedrin and cried out, “⟦Q 186:1.4⟧I have sinned in that I have betrayed innocent blood⟦/Q⟧”, but the leaders mocked him and told him that was his own problem. He threw the silver onto the temple floor and left. The Urantia Book says that at this moment Judas understood what sin really is. Sin is attractive while you are doing it, but afterward only its cold, naked results are left. In despair, Judas finally went alone to a ravine outside the city and took his own life.
p186.007: When Jesus was arrested, he already knew that his work on earth was finished, and he did not care about the details of the trials. He did not answer the false testimony, and he kept silent before Herod, who was only curious. But he always answered clearly when asked whether he was the Son of God, and he spoke to Pilate only when it might help Pilate understand a little more of the truth. Jesus did not try to change the outcome by clever words; he believed it was the Father's will for him to go along with the natural course of human events, like everyone else.
p186.008: Jesus did not lose his calm and dignity even in the face of insults and threats, and he did not grow angry even at the soldiers who mocked and beat him. Instead, he felt sorry for Pilate and tried to shed light into his darkened mind. The Urantia Book says that the trial was really a scene of “⟦Q 186:2.6⟧Pilate on trial before Jesus⟦/Q⟧”. When Pilate cried, “⟦Q 186:2.11⟧Behold the man!⟦/Q⟧” the cry “⟦Q 186:2.11⟧Behold God and man!⟦/Q⟧” echoed throughout the whole universe. All his life Jesus had shown God to people, and now he gave a new revelation of man to God.
p186.010: After Jesus was handed over to the Roman soldiers, the temple guards went to Gethsemane to arrest his followers, but they had all scattered already. The guards burned the empty camp and went back, and the Sanhedrin relaxed, thinking that Jesus' followers were too frightened to do anything. David Zebedee had moved his tent ahead of time and, hidden away, kept up his headquarters for passing on news. Within five minutes he sent messengers off to many places, including Bethsaida, Alexandria, and Damascus, and all that day he sent news every half hour to the apostles and to Jesus' family.
p186.011: David was almost the only follower who took Jesus literally when he said he would “⟦Q 186:3.4⟧rise again on the third day⟦/Q⟧”. When he found that the others did not expect a resurrection so soon, he kept quiet about it, but he arranged for his messengers to gather early Sunday morning at the home of Nicodemus. His simple but dependable preparations would play a big part two days later.
p186.013: After Pilate washed his hands, Jesus was handed over to the Roman soldiers. The soldiers took off the robe Herod had put on him and dressed him in his own clothes again. His friends were in hiding and his enemies had left; even John was not with him, and Jesus was alone with the soldiers. During the half hour they waited to set out, Jesus did not say a word, and The Urantia Book says that at this time the work of the whole universe nearly stopped as everyone watched Urantia. Even the soldiers began to be impressed by Jesus' calm and dignity. The Roman captain decided to execute two thieves who had been sentenced to death along with him, and one of them had heard Jesus teach several times.
p186.014: 5. Jesus’ Death in Relation to the Passover
p186.015: Jesus died around the time the Passover lambs were being offered in the temple, but The Urantia Book explains that Jesus' death had nothing to do with the Jewish system of sacrifices. It was people, not God, who planned and carried out the crucifixion. The Father simply did not interfere in human affairs; he did not require that his Son die in such a way. According to The Urantia Book, by the time of his baptism Jesus had already finished the experience he needed to have on earth, and his life and death after that were all his personal ministry of love, meant to help and lift people up.
p186.016: The Urantia Book also says that Jesus did not die as a sacrifice paying for sin in our place, and that humanity carries no inherited guilt before God. God loved people just as much before Jesus came, and even if Jesus had not died in that way, salvation would have been just as certain. The gospel was revealed far more brightly by his life than by his death. The only thing we need to truly experience that we are children of God is faith that comes from the heart.
p187.002: When the two robbers were ready, twelve soldiers set out for the place of crucifixion under the command of a centurion (a Roman army officer in charge of a hundred soldiers). The two thieves to be executed with Jesus were companions of Barabbas, so Jesus was, in a sense, hanging on the cross in place of Barabbas, who had been set free. The Urantia Book stresses that Jesus accepted this death of his own free will. Jesus had once said, “⟦Q 187:0.3⟧No one takes my life away from me—I lay it down of myself⟦/Q⟧”. Just before nine in the morning, more than two hundred people followed the procession. Some secretly sympathized with Jesus, but most were enemies or onlookers.
p187.004: Jesus walked carrying the crossbeam of the cross on his shoulders. At the front of the procession, a board was carried that Pilate had written in Latin, Greek, and Aramaic: “⟦Q 187:1.2⟧Jesus of Nazareth—the King of the Jews⟦/Q⟧”. The Jewish leaders asked him to change it, but Pilate refused, saying, “⟦Q 187:1.3⟧What I have written, I have written⟦/Q⟧”. To the women weeping by the roadside, Jesus said, “⟦Q 187:1.6⟧weep not for me, but rather weep for yourselves and for your children⟦/Q⟧”, because he was worried about the troubles that would come upon Jerusalem. Showing sympathy to a condemned man was against the law, so these women were truly brave.
p187.005: Jesus had not eaten, drunk, or slept since the Last Supper, and he was worn out by the whipping and the questioning. After passing through the city gate, he finally fell under the weight of the crossbeam, and the centurion made Simon of Cyrene, who was passing by, carry it for him. After watching everything that day, Simon came to believe the gospel, and he went back home to Africa and led his family into the heavenly kingdom. His two sons, Alexander and Rufus, became fine teachers of the gospel.
p187.007: Arriving at Golgotha a little after nine, the soldiers nailed Jesus to the cross. The cross was not high, so Jesus could hear every word of those who mocked him and could see their faces. He was offered drugged wine that the women had prepared to ease his pain, but Jesus did not drink it, because he wanted to keep a clear mind to the very end. The only words Jesus spoke as he was nailed to the cross were, “⟦Q 187:2.4⟧Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do⟦/Q⟧”. The Urantia Book says that the thoughts and motives a person has held all his life are revealed in a moment of crisis.
p187.008: John arrived with Jesus' mother, Mary, his sister Ruth, and his brother Jude, and when Jesus saw them, he smiled. The soldiers divided Jesus' clothes among themselves, and they cast lots for his seamless robe. The Urantia Book says this was actually a good thing. If his followers had kept those clothes, they would have been tempted to worship relics, but Jesus wanted to leave behind not things, but only the memory of a life lived doing the Father's will.
p187.010: Around half past nine, more than a thousand people gathered to see Jesus on the cross. People passing by sneered, “⟦Q 187:3.3⟧If you are the Son of God, why do you not come down from your cross?⟦/Q⟧” and the leaders mocked, “⟦Q 187:3.3⟧He saved others, but himself he cannot save⟦/Q⟧”. When Jesus gave no answer, most of them left as noon drew near, and fewer than fifty remained. Meanwhile, his mother and the women believers quietly stayed near him. When Jesus said, “⟦Q 187:3.5⟧I thirst⟦/Q⟧”, the captain of the guard moistened his lips with a sponge soaked in wine. Jesus chose not to lean on supernatural power, but to die as an ordinary man doing the Father's will.
p187.012: When one robber railed at Jesus, the other robber, who had heard Jesus teach many times, rebuked him. We deserve our punishment, he said, but this man is suffering unjustly. Then he gathered his courage and asked, “⟦Q 187:4.1⟧Lord, remember me when you come into your kingdom⟦/Q⟧”. Jesus promised him, “⟦Q 187:4.1⟧you shall sometime be with me in Paradise⟦/Q⟧”. This young man, who had looked up to Barabbas as a hero, found the true hero on the cross right next to him. The Urantia Book says that if anyone in the crowd had appealed to Jesus in faith, they would have been received with the same love.
p187.013: Around noon, Jesus looked down at his mother and John and said, “⟦Q 187:4.7⟧Woman, behold your son!⟦/Q⟧” and “⟦Q 187:4.7⟧My son, behold your mother!⟦/Q⟧” Then he told the two of them to leave that place. After this, Mary lived at John's home in Bethsaida, and she died less than a year later.
p187.015: After noon, a sandstorm blowing in from the desert darkened the sky, and most of the people who were left went back to the city. As his consciousness faded, Jesus recited verses from the Psalms in his mind, and those standing nearby caught a few words, such as “⟦Q 187:5.2⟧My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?⟦/Q⟧” The Urantia Book explains that Jesus did not feel abandoned by the Father; he was only reciting the twenty-second Psalm, which he knew well.
p187.016: Just before three o'clock, Jesus cried out with a loud voice, “⟦Q 187:5.5⟧It is finished! Father, into your hands I commend my spirit⟦/Q⟧”, and then he breathed his last. When the Roman centurion saw this, he confessed, “⟦Q 187:5.5⟧truly he must have been a Son of God⟦/Q⟧”, and from then on he began to believe in Jesus. The Urantia Book says that Jesus died like a king, just as he had lived, and that he was master of the situation all that day. When the soldiers came to break the legs, Jesus was already dead. Because of his deep anguish of heart, his life ended in less than five and a half hours.
p187.018: At about half past three, David Zebedee sent out his last messengers to announce Jesus' death. John sent the women to the home of Elijah Mark and kept watch at Golgotha until Joseph and Nicodemus, with Pilate's permission, came to take the body. The Urantia Book says that countless beings throughout the universe, watching their beloved Sovereign being crucified, were shocked at how unfeeling people were. Jesus' last moments, forgiving his enemies to the end, welcoming the repentant robber, and caring for his mother, show us that we can choose love even in our hardest moments.
p188.002: The roughly thirty-six hours from three o'clock Friday afternoon to three o'clock Sunday morning, while Jesus' body lay in the tomb, are a time The Urantia Book admits it does not know much about. The Jewish leaders wanted to throw Jesus' body into the common burial pit, as was done with others who were crucified. So Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus went to Pilate and asked him to give them the body. Joseph brought a large sum of money just in case, but Pilate would not take the money and signed the permit right away.
p188.004: When Joseph and Nicodemus reached Golgotha, representatives of the Sanhedrin raised an uproar and tried to take the body. The centurion had his soldiers draw their swords and guard the body, drove the crowd back, and then said to Joseph, “⟦Q 188:1.1⟧This body is yours⟦/Q⟧”. The two men decided to lay Jesus in Joseph's new family tomb, carved out of rock. From that day on, these two former members of the Sanhedrin, who had secretly believed in Jesus, became the boldest followers of Jesus in Jerusalem.
p188.005: At about half past four in the afternoon, Joseph, Nicodemus, John, and the Roman centurion carried the body, wrapped in a linen sheet, to the tomb. They wrapped the body in bandages soaked in myrrh and aloes, laid it on a shelf, and closed the entrance with a stone. Because the Sabbath was coming, everything was done in a hurry, so the Galilean women who had been watching from hiding decided to come back on Sunday morning with spices they would prepare. At this time, about the only followers who truly believed Jesus would rise on the third day were David Zebedee and Joseph.
p188.007: Jesus' followers had forgotten his words that he would rise again on the third day, but his enemies had not. Afraid that the followers would steal the body and spread the word that Jesus had risen, the Jewish leaders asked Pilate to guard the tomb. Pilate gave them ten Roman soldiers, and ten temple guards were added to them. They rolled another stone in front of the tomb and stamped it with Pilate's seal, and twenty guards watched the tomb right up to the moment of the resurrection.
p188.009: During the Sabbath, the followers stayed in hiding, and the nearly one and a half million pilgrims gathered in Jerusalem talked about Jesus' death. Soon they would hear the news of the resurrection and carry it back home. On Saturday night, the eleven apostles gathered again in the upper room of John Mark's home, and his mother, Mary, went back to the family in Bethany.
p188.010: The Urantia Book honestly says it cannot fully explain what happened to Jesus during this time. But it carefully suggests a few things. Jesus' human consciousness probably did not feel time passing, as if he were asleep, so the sleep of death and the resurrection would have followed one another for him like a single moment. It also says that the Thought Adjuster (the divine spirit God sends to live in the human mind) who had lived in Jesus was already personalized and was directing the heavenly hosts on earth. The Urantia Book adds that there is much evidence that, even during this period, the whole of Jesus' personality was not simply asleep without awareness. The Urantia Book also tells us that on the first mansion world (the first world where people wake up after death), a “⟦Q 188:3.11⟧Michael Memorial⟦/Q⟧” has been built in memory of Jesus' life and death on Urantia.
p188.011: 4. Meaning of the Death on the Cross
p188.012: The Urantia Book says clearly that Jesus did not pay for humanity's sins in our place or become a sacrifice to calm an angry God. God is not one who punishes people for their ancestors' wrongdoing, and sin is not something inherited from parents; it is each person's knowing act of going against God's will. Where Moses taught the justice of God, Jesus showed the love and mercy of the Father in heaven.
p188.013: So The Urantia Book says it is better to call Jesus a savior than one who paid a ransom. He showed the way of salvation more clearly and more surely, and he gave the assurance that life continues after death. What matters is not so much the fact that he died, but the way he met death and the spirit in which he did it. A believer's concern should not be just getting saved himself, but loving and serving his neighbors as Jesus did. A true believer worries less about future punishment and more about drifting away from God right now. It is like a wise father who, even when he scolds his child, is trying to set things right with love, not taking out his anger.
p188.015: The cross shows that the relationship between God and people is not that of a king and his subjects, but that of a father and his children. Jesus' love does not stop at simply covering over wrongdoing; it melts away sin and weakness and makes people new. Jesus taught us to overcome evil with good rather than fight against it, and by praying for his enemies, “⟦Q 188:5.6⟧Father, forgive them⟦/Q⟧”, he made the cross a symbol of the victory of love over hate. Stephen, the first martyr, prayed the same kind of prayer as he was being stoned.
p188.016: Jesus did not suffer only on the cross. For more than twenty-five years he had carried the cross of a hard human life. The Urantia Book says there is no greater love than to lay down your life for your friends, but Jesus laid down his life even for his enemies. So no one needs to fear that the Creator does not understand his pain. As we look at the cross, we put down our small complaints and come to want to live for others the way he did.
p189.002: After Jesus was buried, the archangels in charge of resurrection discussed how they might bring Jesus back to life. But they came to the conclusion that a creature cannot help the Creator rise again. Gabriel told them that since Michael (the Son of God who created this universe and was born as the man Jesus) had “⟦Q 189:0.1⟧laid down his life of his own free will, he also had power to take it up again in accordance with his own determination⟦/Q⟧”. The Thought Adjuster (the divine spirit God sends to live in the human mind) who had lived in Jesus also explained to the heavenly hosts that although Jesus had died as a man, he was still alive as the sovereign of the universe, and that he was personally going through every step that human beings go through. Everyone waited breathlessly for that moment.
p189.004: At two minutes past three on Sunday morning, April 9, A.D. 30, the risen Jesus came out of Joseph's tomb in morontia form (the in-between stage of being, between material and spirit). Yet Jesus' physical body was still lying in the tomb, wrapped in linen, and the stone at the entrance and Pilate's seal were untouched. The guards noticed nothing at all. Jesus rose again by the power within himself, without help from anyone. The Urantia Book says that people think matter is everything, but in fact matter is like a shadow of a higher spiritual reality.
p189.005: The Urantia Book sums up the resurrection clearly like this: Jesus' physical body was not part of his risen personality, and he came forth not as a spirit or in the form of the Creator, but in the same morontia form people have when they wake up on the first mansion world after death. The risen Jesus greeted Gabriel and left the affairs of the universe in his hands, and then he told the beings gathered there that he would stay a while in this form to show more of the Father's will.
p189.007: The chief of the archangels said he did not want to watch the body of his beloved Sovereign slowly decay, so he asked permission to return Jesus' physical body to dust at once, and permission was given. To prepare for this, the midwayers (invisible beings between humans and angels) rolled away the great stone from the tomb's entrance, and when the guards saw the stone move by itself, they ran away terrified. The Jewish leaders paid them money to say that the followers had stolen the body while they slept.
p189.008: The Urantia Book explains that the tomb was empty not because Jesus' physical body had come back to life, but because the body went through the natural process of breaking down almost instantly. The empty tomb is a fact, but it is not itself the truth of the resurrection. The real evidence of the resurrection is spiritual, and close to a thousand people met and recognized the risen Jesus in person.
p189.010: Around half past four in the morning, Gabriel gathered the archangels and prepared for the great resurrection that would close an age on Urantia. The risen Jesus gave the command, “⟦Q 189:3.1⟧let the roll call of the planetary resurrection begin⟦/Q⟧”, and as Gabriel's voice rang out, countless people who had been sleeping since the time of Adam woke up in the resurrection halls of the first mansion world. This was the third dispensational resurrection to take place on Urantia. After that, Jesus' Adjuster sent the heavenly hosts back to their posts and departed, and only Gabriel stayed with Jesus.
p189.012: At that hour, the apostles were asleep in the upper room of Mark's home, full of sorrow, fear, and shame, and Thomas had gone somewhere else to grieve alone. A little before three in the morning, five women, including Mary Magdalene, set out for the tomb to anoint Jesus' body with ointment. They worried about who would roll the stone away for them, but when they arrived, the stone had already been moved. Mary bravely went inside, and when she saw that the body was gone and only the bandages and the napkin lay neatly in place, she screamed. The women fled in alarm and then came back.
p189.013: As the women sat there, not knowing what to make of it, a stranger asked, “⟦Q 189:4.10⟧Whom do you seek?⟦/Q⟧” He looked so different that they did not recognize him, but when he called her in a familiar voice, “⟦Q 189:4.10⟧Mary⟦/Q⟧”, she knelt down, exclaiming, “⟦Q 189:4.10⟧My Lord, and my Master⟦/Q⟧”. The Urantia Book explains that human eyes were able to see the morontia form only because of special help from invisible beings. When Mary tried to hold his feet, Jesus said, “⟦Q 189:4.12⟧Touch me not⟦/Q⟧”, and told her that he was no longer as she had known him in the flesh. Then he told them to tell the apostles, and especially Peter, that he had risen. At first the apostles did not believe it, but when Peter heard that his own name had been mentioned, he ran to the tomb with John.
p189.014: 5. Peter and John at the Tomb
p189.015: Peter was afraid to meet the Master, yet he felt hope at the news that a special message had been sent to him. John, being younger, reached the tomb first, and the two of them went in one after the other and saw the grave clothes lying neatly in place. Peter thought someone had stolen the body, but John said that thieves would not have left things so orderly.
p189.016: Meanwhile Mary, discouraged because the apostles would not believe her, came back to the tomb and was weeping, when Jesus appeared to her again and said, “⟦Q 189:5.4⟧Be not doubting; have the courage to believe what you have seen and heard⟦/Q⟧”. When Mary told them again, Peter and John had returned, so the apostles could no longer laugh at her. The fact that the first news of the resurrection went first to someone who grieved the most and stayed close to the very end shows how precious a heart is that never lets go of faith and love.
p190.002: The risen Jesus stayed on this earth for a while and personally experienced the morontia life that people go through on the mansion worlds (the worlds where people wake up after death and grow step by step). The Urantia Book says that believers, too, will rise on the resurrection morning in a morontia body like Jesus' (a body at the in-between stage, between material and spirit). Blood does not flow in this body and it does not eat ordinary food, but it is truly real. So the people who saw the risen Jesus were not fooled by a vision. All the early teachers of the gospel were united by a firm faith in Jesus' resurrection. The Urantia Book also tells us that Mary Magdalene was the spokeswoman for the women believers, just as Peter was the spokesman for the apostles.
p190.004: Because the apostles did not want Jesus to leave, they had taken the promise of resurrection lightly, and they did not believe the women. Joseph of Arimathea and David Zebedee went to the tomb themselves and saw that it was empty. To the apostles, who still doubted, David said, “⟦Q 190:1.3⟧I heard the Master say that, after he should die, he would rise on the third day, and I believe him⟦/Q⟧”, and left. As he went, he put the apostles' money bag, which Judas used to carry, in Matthew's lap.
p190.005: At half past nine in the morning, David gathered his twenty-six messengers, gave them their last assignment, and disbanded the messenger corps. The news they were to carry was, “⟦Q 190:1.5⟧Jesus has risen from the dead; the tomb is empty⟦/Q⟧”. While the apostles stayed in the upper room trembling with fear, these ordinary believers who trusted David became the very first to announce the resurrection, running from Beersheba to Damascus and Alexandria. Afterward David went to Bethany and stayed with Jesus' family, and a few months later he married Ruth, Jesus' youngest sister.
p190.007: After his resurrection, Jesus appeared to believers nineteen times in all, and he did not appear to enemies or to people who could not receive such a meeting spiritually. The third appearance took place around noon on Sunday in Bethany. Jesus' brother James wanted to believe in his brother's mission, but he had long been caught in doubt. As he stood by the empty tomb of Lazarus, he felt as if someone had touched him on the shoulder and turned around. When a strange form said, “⟦Q 190:2.3⟧James, I come to call you to the service of the kingdom⟦/Q⟧”, James recognized his brother Jesus by his voice.
p190.008: A little before two in the afternoon, Jesus appeared before twenty of his family and friends and greeted them, “⟦Q 190:2.6⟧Peace be upon you⟦/Q⟧”, and he asked them tenderly why they had hesitated so long. When they tried to come closer to him, Jesus vanished. David rejoiced, saying, “⟦Q 190:2.5⟧even stronghearted men have begun to see him⟦/Q⟧”.
p190.010: At about a quarter past four in the afternoon, as Mary Magdalene was telling the story of Bethany to twenty-five women believers gathered at Joseph's home, Jesus appeared in their midst. Jesus said that in the kingdom there is no difference between Jew and gentile, rich and poor, man and woman, and he urged the women to spread the gospel to the whole world as well, and to strengthen those who were weak and afraid. And he promised, “⟦Q 190:3.1⟧I will be with you always, even to the ends of the earth⟦/Q⟧”. Of the five appearances up to that day, Mary Magdalene saw four herself.
p190.011: By evening, the rumor that Jesus had risen had spread throughout the whole city. The frightened Sanhedrin hurriedly held a meeting and decided to throw out of the synagogue anyone who spoke of the resurrection. They thought they were finished with Jesus, but The Urantia Book says that the real trouble was only just beginning.
p190.013: At about half past four in the afternoon, Jesus appeared to about forty Greek believers gathered at the home of Flavius. Even though the doors were securely locked, Jesus stood among them and said that the Son of Man had been born among the Jews but had come for all people, and that in the Father's kingdom all are brothers. And he told them to go to the whole world and proclaim the gospel of salvation. The Greeks were filled with awe and stayed awake all night talking about it. Jesus thought a great deal about the apostles, but he waited a little longer so they would have time to look deeply into their own hearts.
p190.015: At about five o'clock that afternoon, Cleopas and Jacob, two shepherd brothers who lived in Emmaus, were arguing on their way home about the rumors of Jesus' empty tomb. The older brother half believed it, and the younger thought it was a trick. Just then Jesus came up and walked with them, but the two did not recognize him. Jesus said, “⟦Q 190:5.4⟧How slow you are to comprehend the truth!⟦/Q⟧” and he explained to them that Jesus' kingdom is not a kingdom of this world but a kingdom of brothers serving one another in the love of God, and that the salvation the Scriptures spoke of means binding up broken hearts and setting free those who are trapped by fear.
p190.016: When they reached their home, the two urged him to stay with them, since it was getting dark. At the table, the moment Jesus broke the bread and handed it to them, their eyes were opened, and just as one said, “⟦Q 190:5.5⟧It is the Master⟦/Q⟧”, Jesus vanished. They said, “⟦Q 190:5.6⟧No wonder our hearts burned within us as he spoke to us while we walked along the road!⟦/Q⟧” and without even eating, they hurried to Jerusalem to tell the apostles the news. This story warmly reminds us that even when we are full of doubt and sorrow, Jesus is quietly walking beside us.
p191.002: Resurrection Sunday was a terrible day for the apostles. Ten of them were hiding in the upper room behind locked doors, afraid of being arrested by the Sanhedrin, and Thomas was alone in Bethpage, lost in his troubles. Each apostle spent that day in his own way. John remembered one by one the words Jesus had spoken about rising again and firmly believed in the resurrection, while Peter swung back and forth between faith and doubt, tormented by the thought that Jesus might not come because Peter had denied him. Nathaniel held the group together with his calm advice, Simon Zelotes was so disappointed that he lay facing the wall, and Philip kept asking whether the marks of the cross would remain on a risen body. The Alpheus twins said simply, “⟦Q 191:0.11⟧our mother says she talked with the Master, and we believe her⟦/Q⟧”.
p191.003: Jesus delayed appearing to the apostles for several reasons. He wanted to give them time to think over the words about death and resurrection he had told them before, to give Peter time to wrestle with his own problems, and he wanted Thomas to be there too at the first appearance. But Thomas was too proud to come back first, and the apostles waited for him. In the end, it was not until the next Saturday evening that Peter and John went to bring him.
p191.005: Around half past eight on Sunday evening, Jesus appeared to Peter as he walked in the garden of Mark's home. This was the eighth morontia manifestation. Morontia means the in-between stage of life, between material and spirit, that mortals pass through after death until they become spirit beings. At the very moment Peter cried out, “⟦Q 191:1.2⟧I believe he has risen from the dead⟦/Q⟧”, Jesus appeared and told him that because he knew Peter had not denied him from the heart, he had already forgiven him even before he asked. And he encouraged him to stop thinking only about himself and his past troubles, and to care less about what he might get from the kingdom and more about what he could give to those who are spiritually poor.
p191.006: Peter ran to the upper room and cried out, “⟦Q 191:1.4⟧I have seen the Master⟦/Q⟧”, and he told them the Master had forgiven him. But when his brother Andrew hinted that Peter had seen things that were not there before, Peter was hurt and fell silent. The Alpheus twins came over and comforted him, saying they believed him.
p191.008: A little after nine that night, while the ten apostles were gathered with all the doors locked, Jesus suddenly appeared in their midst. Greeting them with “⟦Q 191:2.1⟧Peace be upon you⟦/Q⟧”, Jesus gently scolded them for their doubts and arguments, asking whether he had not told them in advance that he would die and rise on the third day. Then he told them that once they were all together again and knew for certain about the resurrection, they should go to Galilee, and he urged them to have faith in God and faith in one another. When Jesus vanished, the apostles fell with their faces to the ground and praised God. This was the ninth appearance.
p191.010: The next day, Monday, Jesus spent the whole day with the morontia creatures who had come to Urantia. Urantia is the name for the earth we live on. More than a million morontia beings had come, along with transition mortals from the mansion worlds; the mansion worlds are the worlds where people first wake up after death to learn and grow. Jesus stayed with them for forty days, sometimes teaching them and sometimes learning about the morontia life that mortals pass through.
p191.011: After that, Jesus' morontia form went up one stage at a time, and in May, after passing through citizenship on Jerusem, he entered the embrace of the Most Highs of Edentia. In this way Michael of Nebadon, Jesus, the Creator Son who made our universe, truly completed his seventh and final bestowal by personally experiencing the life of an ascending mortal.
p191.013: On Tuesday evening, April 11, Jesus appeared before Abner, Lazarus, and about one hundred and fifty believers gathered in the synagogue at Philadelphia. Jesus said that we all have one Father in heaven and that there is only one gospel, the gift of eternal life received by faith. And he told them to fellowship in love with all their brothers who preach the gospel, whether Jew or gentile, Greek or Roman. “⟦Q 191:4.3⟧as you love one another, all men will know that you are my disciples⟦/Q⟧”. Jesus told them to proclaim the fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of men to the whole world, and he promised that he would always be with them, even to the end of the ages.
p191.014: Except for one time in Galilee when more than five hundred saw him, this group was the largest number of people who saw Jesus all at once. The next morning these believers immediately set out to proclaim the resurrection.
p191.016: Thomas had wandered alone in the hills for a week, and on Saturday night he came back to his companions. But even after hearing that they had seen the Master, he stubbornly refused to believe, saying, “⟦Q 191:5.2⟧I will not believe unless I see the Master with my own eyes and put my finger in the mark of the nails⟦/Q⟧”. Right then, in the room with the doors shut, Jesus appeared in front of Thomas. Jesus said that just as the Father had sent him, so he was sending them, and he told them to show God's love not only with words but in their daily lives. They were to love not just people's souls but people themselves, and to love and serve people the way he had loved and served them. Jesus said, “⟦Q 191:5.3⟧I require of my disciples life⟦/Q⟧”.
p191.017: Then Jesus told Thomas that his doubts were most stubborn just before they crumbled, and that he should be not faithless but believing. Thomas fell to his knees and cried, “⟦Q 191:5.5⟧My Lord and my Master!⟦/Q⟧” Jesus said that blessed are those in the ages to come who will believe without having seen. Now the eleven apostles were fully sure of the resurrection, and they left for Galilee before dawn the next day.
p191.019: On the evening of April 18, Jesus also appeared far away in Alexandria, Egypt, to Rodan and about eighty believers. It was the moment when Nathan, David's messenger, was finishing his report of the crucifixion by saying that the Master had promised to rise again. Jesus said that the gospel of the kingdom does not belong to one race, one nation, or a special group of teachers, but to everyone: Jew and gentile, rich and poor, man and woman, and even little children. And he said that if they loved one another and served humankind, people would see the Spirit of Truth in their lives and follow.
p191.020: Two days later, when a messenger came to bring news of the resurrection, the believers there answered, “⟦Q 191:6.4⟧Yes, we know, for we have seen him⟦/Q⟧”. The risen Jesus went to doubting Peter and Thomas one by one and lifted them back up. When we stumble and waver, it is good to remember that love which forgives us first and waits for us.
p192.002: By the time the apostles left for Galilee, the Jewish leaders had grown fairly quiet. Jesus had appeared only to believers, and the apostles were in hiding, so the leaders thought this movement was finished. The spreading rumors of the resurrection made them uneasy, but they trusted that the guards they had bribed would say the followers had carried off the body.
p192.003: From this time on, Peter naturally became the head of the apostles. Jesus had not given him that authority, nor had the apostles elected him, but everyone accepted it because he was the chief preacher. When the apostles left for Galilee early Monday morning, young John Mark secretly followed them, and when they were well past Bethany, he boldly joined them. The apostles stopped many times along the way to tell about the risen Master, so they did not reach Bethsaida until late Wednesday night.
p192.005: At dawn on Friday, April 21, the apostles were coming back to Bethsaida after fishing all night without catching a single fish. Someone standing by a fire on the beach asked, “⟦Q 192:1.3⟧Lads, have you caught anything?⟦/Q⟧” When they said no, he told them to cast the net on the right side of the boat, and when they did, the net was filled. John Zebedee recognized him first and whispered, “⟦Q 192:1.3⟧It is the Master⟦/Q⟧”, and impulsive Peter jumped straight into the water. John Mark ran down the beach and knelt at the Master's feet, and Jesus, unlike in Jerusalem, said in a very ordinary way, “⟦Q 192:1.4⟧Well, John, I am glad to see you again⟦/Q⟧”.
p192.006: Peter hesitated for a moment when he saw the charcoal fire on the beach. It reminded him of the charcoal fire he had warmed himself by in the courtyard of Annas on the night he denied the Master. But he soon pulled himself together and knelt down. They had caught 153 large fish, and The Urantia Book explains that this was not a miracle but the foreknowledge of the Master, who knew ahead of time where the fish were. Jesus cooked the fish himself, broke the bread and handed it out, and talked about old memories.
p192.007: Meanwhile, Simon Zelotes was so discouraged that when they reached Bethsaida he left his companions and went home. Jesus told them to send two men to bring him back, and Peter and Andrew took on that task.
p192.008: 2. Visiting with the Apostles Two and Two
p192.009: After breakfast, Jesus walked along the beach and talked with the apostles two at a time. He asked John, “⟦Q 192:2.1⟧do you love me?⟦/Q⟧” and then told him to give up his narrow-mindedness and show with his life that love is the greatest thing in the world. He asked Peter the same question three times. When Peter, feeling hurt, said, “⟦Q 192:2.4⟧Lord, you know all things⟦/Q⟧”, and so he knew Peter truly loved him, Jesus said, “⟦Q 192:2.4⟧Feed my sheep⟦/Q⟧”, and told him to care for the weak, the poor, and the young and to follow him to the end. When Peter asked what would happen to John, Jesus told him not to worry about his brothers' affairs but only to make sure that he himself followed him.
p192.010: He asked Andrew and James, “⟦Q 192:2.7⟧do you trust me?⟦/Q⟧” He told Andrew to trust his brothers more, including Peter, and to be a wise counselor to Jesus' brother James, who would later be put in charge of the church. He told James that if he trusted the Master more, he would be less impatient with his brothers, and that he should cultivate patience. He asked Thomas and Nathaniel, “⟦Q 192:2.9⟧do you serve me?⟦/Q⟧” He told Thomas to stop doubting and believe in God like a child, and he told Nathaniel to add friendship to his advice and love to his philosophy, and to be less critical.
p192.011: He asked Philip and Matthew, “⟦Q 192:2.11⟧do you obey me?⟦/Q⟧” To these two, who had been in charge of supplies and money, he said that they were now free of that work and should preach the gospel without fear. To the Alpheus twins he said that even if they went back to their old work, they should keep their faith, saying, “⟦Q 192:2.13⟧Nothing which a son of God does can be common⟦/Q⟧”. Jesus told them to meet him at noon the next day on the mount of ordination, and then he vanished.
p192.013: At noon on Saturday, April 22, the eleven apostles gathered near Capernaum on the very mountain where Jesus had first made them apostles. When Jesus appeared, the apostles knelt in a circle, and Jesus repeated the same charge and the same scene as at their first ordination. But this time his prayer was different; it was in the majestic voice of one who had received the power and authority of the whole universe, and the apostles never forgot this experience as long as they lived. For a week after that Jesus did not appear, and the apostles waited in Bethsaida, wondering whether the Master had already gone to the Father.
p192.015: On Saturday, April 29, more than five hundred believers gathered by the shore at Bethsaida to hear Peter's first public sermon after the resurrection. When Peter finished by saying, “⟦Q 192:4.3⟧we proclaim that we have seen him and talked with him⟦/Q⟧”, Jesus appeared right beside him in full view of everyone, said, “⟦Q 192:4.3⟧Peace be upon you⟦/Q⟧”, and vanished. This was the fifteenth appearance.
p192.016: The apostles went back to Jerusalem, but a few hours before they arrived, John Mark's father, Elijah Mark, suddenly died. The apostles grieved the loss of a faithful friend, and they kept using the upper room of John Mark's home as their headquarters. And all of them except a few pledged to proclaim the risen Master publicly. The Urantia Book explains that from this time on, the gospel of sonship with God and the brotherhood of men began to shift toward proclaiming Jesus' resurrection. Nathaniel objected, but he could not hold back Peter's enthusiasm. In this way, “⟦Q 192:4.8⟧the religion of Jesus⟦/Q⟧” slowly turned into a “⟦Q 192:4.8⟧religion about Jesus⟦/Q⟧”. Just like the personal words Jesus gave to each apostle, each of us is called to know our own shortcomings and to grow little by little.
p193.002: On Friday night, May 5, in the courtyard of Nicodemus in Jerusalem, the eleven apostles, the women's corps, and about fifty disciples gathered together for the first time since the resurrection. While they were talking, Jesus appeared before them all and began to teach. Jesus said that although he had told them in advance that he would die and rise again, they were surprised because they had heard the words without understanding what they meant. And he reminded them again that his only purpose had been to show the Father in heaven to his children.
p193.003: Jesus especially urged them: “⟦Q 193:0.4⟧Your message is not changed by my resurrection experience⟦/Q⟧”. What the apostles were to proclaim was not just the story of the resurrection, but the whole gospel: that God is our Father and all people are his sons. Jesus told them that just as he had shown God through love and service, they too should show God to people through loving service, and he told them to stay in Jerusalem until the Spirit of Truth came. The believers talked over these words until dawn.
p193.005: On the Sabbath afternoon of May 13, Jesus appeared to about seventy-five Samaritan believers in Sychar in Samaria, near Jacob's well, where he had once told a woman named Nalda about the water of life. Jesus said that the time had come to worship God in spirit and in truth, not on some particular mountain or in a temple, but where you are, “⟦Q 193:1.2⟧as you are⟦/Q⟧”. He said that salvation is God's free gift received by faith, but that it must be followed by the experience of bearing fruit in your life. If you accept God as your Father, you also accept all people as your brothers, and since brothers are family, you must love and serve them like family. The Samaritans were amazed and spread the news to every nearby village.
p193.007: On May 16, he appeared to believers in Tyre in Phoenicia. Jesus explained that the fact that the dead rise is not itself the gospel; it is only part of the result of believing the gospel. And he said that the life of a person born of the spirit bears fruit. That fruit includes loving service, unselfish devotion, courageous loyalty, honesty, undying hope, mercy, goodness, forgiveness, and lasting peace. Jesus said that we can enter the kingdom like little children, but the Father wants us to grow in grace and become spiritual adults. This news soon spread to Sidon, Antioch, and Damascus.
p193.009: On Thursday morning, May 18, Jesus appeared for the last time to the eleven apostles as they were about to have breakfast in the upper room. When Simon Zelotes asked whether the kingdom would now be restored, Jesus said that he was still bound by the old idea of a material kingdom and that he would soon receive spiritual power. And he urged them again and again to love one another and to trust one another. Judas had fallen away, he said, because his love grew cold and he did not trust his brothers. Jesus said that even while he was in the flesh, he did not stay alone for long, and that he had sent his followers out two by two to guard them against the harm of loneliness and isolation. Then he silently led the apostles toward the Mount of Olives.
p193.011: Here The Urantia Book looks back at why Judas fell. The biggest reason was that Judas had an isolated personality that did not share his heart with others, and he did not grow in love and in spiritual things. Thomas and Nathaniel were also full of doubts and very individualistic, but as time went on they came to love and trust Jesus and their companions more and more. Judas, on the other hand, when he was troubled, looked for comfort not from his friends but from people who were indifferent or hostile to the kingdom.
p193.012: The weaknesses of Judas that The Urantia Book points out are these: he chose to shut himself off; he had grown up too comfortably as a child and could not stand losing; and whenever he was disappointed, he always blamed others. He held grudges and thought about revenge, he would not face the facts honestly, and he did not share his troubles even with friends who truly loved him. In all the years they spent together, he never once went to Jesus with a personal problem. The Urantia Book says, “⟦Q 193:4.13⟧In life, he ignored those who loved him, and in death, he was friendless⟦/Q⟧”.
p193.014: Around half past seven in the morning, Jesus and the eleven apostles reached the western slope of the Mount of Olives, overlooking Jerusalem and Gethsemane. Without being told to, the apostles knelt in a circle around Jesus. Jesus told them to wait in Jerusalem, because he would soon send the Spirit of Truth, and he urged them, “⟦Q 193:5.2⟧Love men with the love wherewith I have loved you⟦/Q⟧”, and to serve them. Then, with the word “⟦Q 193:5.2⟧Farewell⟦/Q⟧”, he vanished.
p193.015: The Urantia Book explains that the so-called ascension was no different from the other times during those forty days when he had vanished from sight. Jesus passed through Jerusem and Edentia, was released from the morontia state, and on Salvington, the headquarters of our universe, took up again his full sovereignty as the Creator Son.
p193.017: Peter soon called together one hundred and twenty of the leading disciples in Jerusalem at the home of Mary Mark. Jesus' mother, Mary, and his brother James were there as well. Peter told vividly about the Master's farewell and ascension, and the apostles cast lots and chose Matthias as a new apostle in Judas's place.
p193.018: After that, the apostles' paths slowly went different ways. The twins went back to their homes in Galilee, and Nathaniel, who disagreed with Peter's preaching about Jesus, went by way of Philadelphia to distant lands to preach the gospel as he understood it. The apostles who stayed in Jerusalem and first proclaimed the gospel were six: Peter, Andrew, James, John, Philip, and Matthew. Peter urged everyone to pray as they prepared to receive the spirit promised to all believers. Looking at the different paths of Judas and Thomas, it is good to think about how important it is, in hard times, to open your heart and walk alongside a trustworthy friend.
p194.002: At about one o'clock in the afternoon, the one hundred and twenty believers praying in the upper room sensed a strange presence in the room. At the same time, all of them felt a new and deep joy, security, and confidence, and a strong desire rose up in them to go out and tell the gospel. Peter declared that this was the Spirit of Truth the Master had promised, the spirit Jesus sends into people's hearts, and he said they should go to the temple and tell the good news.
p194.003: But here The Urantia Book points out something important. The gospel they had been taught to preach was that God is our Father and that all people are his sons and brothers of one another. Yet in this moment overflowing with joy, the greatest news they could think of was the fact that the Master had risen. So without realizing it, they slipped into the mistake of putting some of the facts connected with the gospel in the place of the gospel itself, and this trend continued from Peter all the way to Paul. The Urantia Book explains that while the gospel of the kingdom is “⟦Q 194:0.7⟧the fatherhood of God⟦/Q⟧” and “⟦Q 194:0.7⟧the brotherhood of men⟦/Q⟧”, the Christianity that developed afterward centered on the experience of fellowship between the believer and the risen Christ. Considering the situation, it is understandable that they came to preach a new gospel about Jesus.
p194.005: This day happened to be the Jewish festival of Pentecost, so thousands of people from all over the world were in Jerusalem. The apostles, who had been hiding for forty days, appeared boldly in the temple, and Peter stood in the very spot where Jesus had last taught and made a passionate appeal. Six apostles spoke for more than an hour and a half in Greek, Hebrew, and Aramaic, and more than two thousand people came to believe. The Jewish leaders were astonished, but there were so many believers that they could not lay a hand on them. The new believers were baptized in the Master's name at the pool of Siloam. Even so, they had not yet left Judaism; they still lived as a group within it.
p194.007: While Jesus was on earth, he taught a gospel that freed people from the superstition that they are evil by nature and helped them realize their dignity as sons of God. Now Jesus was gone, but in his place he sent the Spirit of Truth. This spirit lives within people and, in every generation, speaks Jesus' message anew in a way that fits that age. The work of the Spirit of Truth is to help people understand truth, to keep believers from feeling alone like orphans, and to help them remember and understand the Master's words. This spirit does not draw attention to itself but only makes us aware of Jesus, so you can tell whether you are with that spirit by the experience of a deepening fellowship with Jesus.
p194.008: The Urantia Book says that Jesus did not live as a model for everyone to copy word for word, but showed the life of a person submitted to the Father's will. Yet that life and death soon turned into a new gospel that he had rescued people by paying a ransom. Even so, this new message carried many of the truths of the original gospel, and in less than a month after receiving the spirit, the apostles grew spiritually more than they had in four years of living with Jesus.
p194.009: Since the Spirit of Truth came, people receive the help of three spirits: the Thought Adjuster, the spirit of the Father, a fragment of God who lives in our minds; the Spirit of Truth, the spirit of the Son; and the Holy Spirit. In this way, the Spirit of Truth brought to this world the last of the spirit gifts that help us on our journey upward in search of God.
p194.011: The Urantia Book says that Pentecost has been misunderstood as an event of overflowing, excited emotions. The main work of the Spirit of Truth is to teach the love of the Father and the mercy of the Son. Just as Jesus showed God in the flesh, the Spirit of Truth shows Jesus in our hearts. So after Pentecost, Jesus could live anew in the life of every believer. In the world there are many times when lies and injustice seem to win, but just as the resurrection morning and an even brighter Pentecost came after the dark day of the cross, faith wins in the end. The religion of Jesus is not a religion that helps you escape from life; it is a religion, built on faith, hope, and love, that lifts up this life right now.
p194.012: The Spirit of Truth was given not only to the apostles but to every man and woman in the upper room and to every honest person in the whole world. Jesus' mother and brother received no more than anyone else. In this way Pentecost erased all religious discrimination based on race, nation, culture, social rank, or sex, and it also overturned the idea that you can receive the spirit only through special priests, holy places, or set ceremonies. As the saying goes, “⟦Q 194:3.5⟧Where the spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty⟦/Q⟧”. Now true religion shows itself within each individual soul.
p194.013: Pentecost also gave people the power to forgive hurts, the power to stay gentle even in the face of injustice, and the power to meet hate with love. The Urantia Book says that in all the destructive wars humankind has been through, the only victor was the gospel of Jesus, which overcomes evil with good. Before Pentecost, people searched for God; now the fact shone out that God also comes looking for people and sends his spirit into them. Prayer did not make the spirit come, but sincere prayer digs the channels for that gift to flow in wider and deeper.
p194.015: When Jesus was crucified, the apostles completely fell apart, but through the resurrection and Pentecost they were changed into brave men following a living Lord. The early believers met together every day with one heart, broke bread, prayed, called one another brothers and sisters, and shared what they had. But their message shifted toward proclaiming the risen Christ and his soon return. The Urantia Book says this was more a fellowship of believers in Jesus than a fellowship of brothers in the family of the Father in heaven, but it also says that even this was the greatest religion humankind had ever known. However, selling all their property and sharing it, in the belief that the Master would return soon, eventually led to poverty and hardship.
p194.016: When the Sadducees put the leaders in prison, Rabbi Gamaliel advised leaving them alone, saying that if this work came from men it would fall apart, but if it came from God it could not be stopped. But Stephen, a Greek believer from Alexandria, who taught something closer to Jesus' teachings, was stoned and became the first martyr. Because of this, the believers separated from Judaism and founded the church in Jerusalem under Peter's leadership, and those who scattered to escape persecution carried the gospel by way of Antioch to Rome and to the ends of the empire. It is good to remember that the spirit of Pentecost is still quietly trying, for anyone and everywhere, to show Jesus to our hearts.
p195.002: After Pentecost, Peter became the real founder of the Christian church, Paul carried this message to the gentiles, and Greek believers spread it throughout the whole Roman Empire. The people of the Western world at that time had inherited the brilliant philosophy and art of Greece, but they had no religion to fill their hearts, so they were spiritually hungry. Christianity came to such people as a new way of life, and after clashing with the existing religions, it eventually moved toward compromise.
p195.003: The Urantia Book names the reasons Christianity spread so quickly: Paul's excellent organization, its taking in the good points of Greek philosophy, and above all the great ideals that rang out from the life of Jesus. The leaders compromised with other religions and even took on the splendor of their rituals, but in return they gave the world higher moral standards, a broader idea of God, the hope of living forever, and Jesus of Nazareth. The Urantia Book says that these compromised ideals of the Master “⟦Q 195:0.12⟧are still latent in his gospel⟦/Q⟧”, and that someday they will show their full power.
p195.005: Christianity's meeting with Greek culture began on the day Paul spoke in Athens about “⟦Q 195:1.1⟧the Unknown God⟦/Q⟧”. The Greeks taught political freedom and Jesus taught spiritual freedom, and when these two ideas came together, they formed a mighty foundation for human freedom. The Greeks treasured beauty and the Jews treasured holiness, but both peoples loved truth. The Greeks were looking for one greater and better God, and wherever Greek culture had spread, Christianity took root. The Urantia Book adds that the Eastern stream, which was more faithful to Jesus' teachings, did not spread very widely.
p195.007: Rome was tolerant of foreign languages, peoples, and religions. The early persecutions happened because Christians used the word “⟦Q 195:2.2⟧kingdom⟦/Q⟧”, and so were mistaken for political rivals. The Romans were honest and had strong self-control, but they had no religion worthy of the name, so they accepted Christianity as a moral philosophy. In many cases, however, it became the moral culture of society rather than personal spiritual growth. Even so, many people found, beneath that outward form, the real truth that feeds the soul.
p195.009: Rome gave political unity, Greece gave unity of culture and learning, and Christianity gave religious unity. To people who did not even have a word for “⟦Q 195:3.3⟧unselfishness⟦/Q⟧”, Christianity brought new comfort and freedom. Its greatest power came from the way believers, even under persecution, lived lives of service and died for their faith. The teaching that Christ loves children also put an end to the custom of abandoning unwanted babies. But The Urantia Book explains that this religion came too late to stop the decline of the empire that had already begun, and it did not save the empire spiritually.
p195.011: During Europe's so-called Dark Ages, the church declined along with society, because it was tied up with society and politics. Religion became a rigid, monastery-centered form, and individual people almost disappeared before the authority and traditions of the church. Even so, Christianity endured the long night and kept its moral influence, and after the Renaissance it came back to life in many denominations. The Urantia Book says this long history shows that Christianity has great power to recover, and that even in the face of the new challenge of an age of science and materialism, the religion of Jesus will win in the end.
p195.013: The more civilization advances, the more we need the attitude to “⟦Q 195:5.1⟧seek first the realities of heaven⟦/Q⟧”. Religion is a personal spiritual experience, different from logic, from the sense of beauty, and even from ethics or morals, and it reaches its height in worship. The Urantia Book says that a society without morals based on spiritual reality cannot hold together, any more than a solar system without gravity.
p195.014: The Urantia Book also gives us warm advice. Do not rush to satisfy all your curiosity and love of adventure in this one short life; be patient and wait for the endless adventures that lie ahead. It also says that the evil in the world is only a black spot on the white background of good, so rather than talking a lot about evil, we should share the good truth. The truest guide that leads us to insight into God is love.
p195.016: The Urantia Book says that science has unintentionally driven people into materialistic anxiety, but that humanity's spiritual resources can never run dry. True religion has no reason to fight with science. Science measures quantities and deals with phenomena, while religion deals with origins, values, and goals. All that science has destroyed are childish illusions; it has not touched the teachings of Jesus shown in the lives of believers.
p195.017: Truth, beauty, and goodness are not found inside physics or chemistry. A machine cannot know truth or treasure goodness. The Urantia Book points out that one of the great problems of modern people is that they think they are too busy to make time for spiritual meditation. And it says, “⟦Q 195:6.16⟧when you once start out to find God, that is the conclusive proof that God has already found you⟦/Q⟧”.
p195.019: The Urantia Book explains the weakness of materialism like this: if people were really only machines, they could not even know that they are machines. A machine cannot measure or evaluate itself, and it does not dream, picture ideals, or thirst for truth. So the self-conscious person who claims, ‘I am a machine,’ is himself the best argument against that claim.
p195.020: Facts never clash with true faith, but theories can. Science should do on the material side what religion does: widen the horizons of life and help people grow bigger. It is not science but the scientist, not art but the artist, not religion but the religious person who shows a higher reality. The Urantia Book encourages us not to be swept along by the currents of material things, but to row hard and become people who change the current.
p195.022: The Urantia Book explains that secularism, the movement that tries to live without God, was born out of atheistic science and as a reaction against the medieval church, which had controlled everything. Secularism freed people from the bonds of the church and bore good fruit, such as tolerance, democratic government, and civil liberties. The Urantia Book tells us not to throw away these benefits hastily. But as secularism turned its back even on God, the danger arose that it would hand people over once again to the bondage of a dictator state.
p195.023: The Urantia Book says that you cannot build the brotherhood of men while ignoring the fatherhood of God. Freedom or wealth without God does not bring peace, and it explains that the tragedy of the world war in the early twentieth century was a terrible harvest of materialism and secularism. We do not need to give up faith in God in order to enjoy tolerance and freedom.
p195.025: The Urantia Book tells us not to neglect the river of truth that has flowed down through the centuries, our spiritual heritage. Throw away superstition, it says, but hold on firmly to eternal truth. Christianity needs to meet the uncompromising teachings of Jesus anew, and religion needs new spiritual leaders who will depend only on Jesus and his teachings.
p195.026: The Urantia Book says that many people today avoid the religion of Jesus because they are afraid it will change them. In fact, the religion of Jesus asks us to devote our lives to knowing God's will and to serve people unselfishly. What the world needs is not a secondhand religion we hear about from others, but a religion we experience for ourselves. Just as words describing something beautiful cannot match the thrill of seeing it yourself, the experience of knowing God personally lifts the soul higher than doctrine does.
p195.028: The Urantia Book says that Christianity has made a great contribution to the world, but what the world needs most now is Jesus. The world needs to see Jesus living again in the lives of people born of the spirit. “⟦Q 195:10.4⟧The kingdom of God is within you⟦/Q⟧” is one of the greatest things Jesus ever said. What changes the world is not the first mile, walked out of duty or custom, but the second mile of freely serving in love, and The Urantia Book laments that far too few people actually walk that road.
p195.029: The Urantia Book says that although Jesus did not found the church, he has nurtured it as the best available representative of his work. And it says that even with its many faults, twentieth-century Christianity was one of the greatest forces for good, so it should not be taken lightly. The true church, the brotherhood of Jesus, is marked not by uniformity, where everyone becomes the same, but by spiritual unity, connected to the living Jesus.
p195.030: The Urantia Book says that if the church bravely follows the Master's plan, countless young people who seemed indifferent will rush forward to join this adventure. It also says that education should teach how to build character rather than self-satisfaction. The hope of Christianity lies in learning anew the living gospel of the fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of man. Each one of you can be a young person who walks that second mile.
p196.002: Jesus believed in God with his whole heart. He went through all the joys and sorrows that people go through, but he never once doubted that God was caring for him and leading him. His faith was not a matter of following tradition or understanding with the head alone; it was a very personal, living faith that grew out of his fellowship with the spirit of God living in his mind, the Thought Adjuster. To Jesus, God was holy and great, and at the same time “⟦Q 196:0.2⟧The living and loving Father in heaven⟦/Q⟧”.
p196.003: Jesus did not cling to faith in order to forget hard things. Even in the middle of difficulties he was at peace, because he trusted God deeply, and he enjoyed the joy of living with the Father. The Urantia Book says that Jesus' greatest gift to humanity was not so much teaching many new ideas about God as showing, with his life, a living faith in God. His faith was very strong, but it never turned into fanaticism, and it was always in harmony with his responsibilities to his family, his work, and his neighbors.
p196.004: For Jesus, prayer was not a duty. Prayer was a sincere conversation in which he expressed thanks, sorted out his thoughts, found courage, and gave himself over to the Father's will. Jesus trusted God the way a child trusts its parents, but his faith was not childish; it grew along with an adult's wise courage and rose so high that it had no fear. That is why Jesus does not simply ask his followers to believe in him; he invites them to “⟦Q 196:0.13⟧believe with him⟦/Q⟧”. This is the full meaning of the words “⟦Q 196:0.13⟧Follow me⟦/Q⟧”.
p196.006: The Urantia Book says that we must not look at Jesus only as the glorified Christ and lose sight of the man Jesus. Jesus was the most truly religious man in this world, a man who knew God's will by faith and did it. The greatest religious teacher in the world was not a priest but an ordinary man, and that is why people gladly listened to him.
p196.007: Following Jesus does not mean copying his outward ways exactly; it means believing in God as he believed in God and believing in people as he believed in people. Jesus did not argue or debate about the fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of men; he simply lived them and showed them. The Urantia Book says that Jesus, like us, climbed step by step from human consciousness to the realization of divinity, with the help of faith and the Thought Adjuster, and it describes these seven stages, from the arrival of the Adjuster, through his baptism, the Mount of Transfiguration, and the resurrection and ascension, to the final embrace of the Father.
p196.009: The Urantia Book says, “⟦Q 196:2.1⟧You may preach a religion about Jesus, but, perforce, you must live the religion of Jesus⟦/Q⟧”. The gospel of the kingdom was founded on Jesus' own religious experience, while Christianity was founded mainly on Paul's experience. People came to worship the divine Christ, but the man Jesus, who bravely walked the path of faith until he became one with God, was largely forgotten. The Urantia Book says that Jesus was truly man and truly God, and that his life is a living way that everyone can walk.
p196.010: Jesus did not see the world as basically evil, and he helped people live comfortably in this world. He saw most people as weak rather than wicked, as confused rather than depraved, and whatever their situation, he regarded them all as children of God and his own brothers. Because Jesus valued people so highly, he was glad to pour himself out in serving them. Could anyone fail to be moved by the faith Jesus has in you?
p196.012: The Urantia Book says that a living religious experience is a power that solves many of life's difficulties. Religion does not make problems disappear, but it shines light on them and helps us rise above them. People are educated by facts, ennobled by wisdom, and saved by faith. There are three proofs that God's spirit lives within us: that we can love others without expecting anything back, that we can realize the universe is friendly to us, and that we can worship God.
p196.013: Spiritual joy cannot be seen under a microscope, and love cannot be weighed on a scale, but they are real. The Urantia Book says that if the Hebrews had a religion of morality and the Greeks a religion of beauty, Jesus showed a religion of love: the security of living in the Father's love and the joy of sharing that love with our neighbors. The Urantia Book explains that morality is the soil in which religion grows, but morality alone cannot show the ultimate good; religion makes morality higher and more meaningful. It also says that while art seeks beauty, science seeks the mysteries of the universe, and philosophy seeks the meaning of life as a whole, religion is a person's highest reaching out to find God and to become like him. It adds that some people's lives are too great and noble to stop at merely being successful. And The Urantia Book tells us, “⟦Q 196:3.33⟧Be not discouraged⟦/Q⟧”. Humanity is still growing, and the revelation of God given through Jesus will not fail.
p196.014: We have now come to the last paper of The Urantia Book. The Urantia Book says that the greatest adventure of our lives is growing closer in friendship with the God who lives in our hearts, and it ends by saying that the idea of God as Father remains the highest concept of God that human beings have. You can begin this adventure too. As Jesus did, try believing in God as your Father and in the people beside you as your brothers and sisters. It is all right to make mistakes and to fall. God came looking for you first, is always with you, and is waiting for you to grow into your very best self.
